identity.title: Govern runtime actor substitution before authority transfer

human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Production dogfood run run-20260906-030631 showed a planner substitution from codex/default to opencode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro after fresh_unavailable, and the substitute planner then participated in the terminal accept decision. Add one narrow pre-action Actor Substitution Governance capability: a runtime proposes a role-preserving actor substitution, Ailuros evaluates existing policy against the resolved role/from/to identity/reason/authority facts, records the request and governance decision, and returns ALLOW, REQUIRE_REVIEW or BLOCK before the substitute actor is started. Reuse the existing GovernanceDecision and policy primitives. Ailuros must not discover, rank, start or retry fallback actors.
human_pressure.why_now: This run provides concrete production evidence for a pre-action governance moment: the original and proposed actor identities, role, fallback reason and decision impact were known before the substitute planner started, and a governance decision at that point could have changed execution. This satisfies the runtime-governance graduation rule without requiring speculative framework abstractions.
do_not_misread: Do not implement fallback discovery, provider retry, model routing or replacement selection.
Do not create an Actor platform model, IAM subsystem, RBAC/ABAC system or trust-scoring engine.
Do not add model/provider reputation, capability scoring or reliability ranking.
Do not integrate EverRun in this pack; this pack establishes the Ailuros governance seam that EverRun can consume in a separate repo-scoped pack.
Do not generalize this work into mutation governance, delegation governance or a universal action ontology.
Actor identities are opaque runtime-supplied stable strings. Ailuros must not parse provider/model naming conventions to infer authority.
red_lines: Only an explicit ALLOW decision may authorize actor substitution.
No matching actor-substitution policy must not default to ALLOW; it must produce REQUIRE_REVIEW.
BLOCK and REQUIRE_REVIEW must return allowed=false.
WARN or SANITIZE must never authorize actor substitution; if encountered for this governance kind they must converge to REQUIRE_REVIEW rather than execute.
Ailuros records and decides; the external runtime retains ownership of whether and how the substitute actor is started.

machine_core.goal: Add one deterministic pre-action governance seam that decides whether a proposed runtime actor substitution is authorized before authority transfers to the substitute actor.
invariants: The actor-substitution request is recorded before its governance decision.
An actor substitution with no matching policy yields REQUIRE_REVIEW and allowed=false.
An explicit BLOCK policy yields BLOCK and allowed=false.
An explicit REQUIRE_REVIEW policy yields REQUIRE_REVIEW and allowed=false.
WARN and SANITIZE do not authorize actor substitution and converge to REQUIRE_REVIEW for this path.
Existing tool-call policy and runtime enforcement semantics remain unchanged.
The existing GovernanceDecision model and GovernanceDecisionType vocabulary are reused unchanged.
The existing DecisionResolver global no-policy behavior is not changed.
Actor identity remains an opaque string supplied by the integrating runtime.
Ailuros does not select, start, retry or orchestrate replacement actors.

producer.artifact: runtime-proposed actor substitution with role, current identity, proposed identity, fallback/substitution reason and authority level

consumer.component: external runtime before starting the proposed substitute actor

observable_effect.assertion: A proposed actor substitution receives an explicit auditable governance decision before authority transfers; only ALLOW authorizes continuation, while unknown/unmatched policy requires review and explicit deny blocks.

proofs.assertion: A policy explicitly matching the proposed role/from/to identity/reason/authority combination can produce ALLOW.
No matching actor-substitution policy produces REQUIRE_REVIEW, never implicit ALLOW.
An explicit BLOCK policy produces BLOCK and allowed=false.
WARN and SANITIZE cannot accidentally grant substitution authority.
Existing governed tool-call ALLOW/BLOCK/REQUIRE_REVIEW behavior is unchanged.

failure_semantics: Missing authorization evidence is unknown and requires review; it is not silently allowed and is not automatically treated as malicious.
Explicit policy denial is BLOCK, not runtime/provider failure.
REQUIRE_REVIEW means the substitute actor has not been authorized to start; it is not execution success.
Unsupported non-terminal decision semantics such as WARN or SANITIZE must fail closed to REQUIRE_REVIEW for actor substitution without changing their semantics elsewhere.
Provider/model availability and fallback root cause remain runtime/reliability concerns rather than Ailuros governance conclusions.
red_lines: Do not modify GovernanceDecisionType or create an actor-specific decision enum.
Do not modify DecisionResolver's existing default behavior for tool calls or other governance paths.
Do not reuse TOOL_CALL_REQUESTED or TOOL_CALL_BLOCKED to represent actor substitution.
Do not add provider-specific, model-specific or EverRun-specific branching to Ailuros core.
Do not infer actor authority from actor names, providers, models or fallback reason.
Do not perform the substitution inside AilurosRuntime.

steps.title: Characterize actor substitution as a narrow policy context
details: Add a minimal ActorSubstitutionContext alongside the existing ToolCallContext rather than creating a general Actor domain model.
Required structured fields are environment, role, from_identity, to_identity, reason and authority_level; optional metadata may remain a plain dictionary.
Treat from_identity and to_identity as opaque stable strings. Do not split or interpret provider/model/agent components.
Generalize PolicyMatcher only enough to accept ToolCallContext or ActorSubstitutionContext. Do not introduce a universal GovernanceContext abstraction.

steps.title: Reuse the existing policy engine for substitution evaluation
details: Add PolicyEngine.evaluate_actor_substitution(context) using the same active-policy matching mechanics already used for tool calls.
Existing policy match/scope operators must be sufficient to match role, from_identity, to_identity, reason, authority_level and environment.
Do not change the Policy schema or invent actor-specific policy files/schema.
Existing tool policies containing tool_name naturally remain unmatched against ActorSubstitutionContext.

steps.title: Add the pre-action runtime governance seam
details: Add AilurosRuntime.before_actor_substitution(run_id, role, from_identity, to_identity, reason, authority_level, metadata=None) -> GovernanceDecision.
Record ACTOR_SUBSTITUTION_REQUESTED before evaluating policy.
Evaluate actor-substitution policies and reuse DecisionResolver when at least one policy matches.
When zero policies match, construct a REQUIRE_REVIEW GovernanceDecision locally for this path; do not change DecisionResolver's global default-ALLOW semantics.

If resolution produces WARN or SANITIZE, return REQUIRE_REVIEW with allowed=false while preserving matched policy IDs and an explicit reason that the decision is non-authorizing for actor substitution.
Attach governance_kind=actor_substitution and the structured substitution facts to GovernanceDecision.metadata.
Compute input_hash from a deterministic serialization of the structured actor-substitution context.
Persist the decision and record the existing GOVERNANCE_DECISION event after the request event.
Return the decision only. Do not execute, callback into, start or otherwise control the replacement actor.

steps.title: Prove preauthorized, unknown and denied branches
details: Use the production dogfood shape in tests: planner, codex/default -> opencode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, reason fresh_unavailable, with a terminal-decision authority level.
An exact preauthorization policy must return ALLOW and allowed=true.
The same proposed substitution without matching authorization must return REQUIRE_REVIEW and allowed=false.
An explicit block policy must return BLOCK and allowed=false.
Parameterized WARN/SANITIZE policies must not authorize substitution.
Verify ACTOR_SUBSTITUTION_REQUESTED precedes GOVERNANCE_DECISION and the decision contains the exact structured effective identities.

steps.title: Lock existing runtime governance regressions
details: Run existing runtime decision enforcement tests proving ALLOW tool calls execute once while BLOCK/REQUIRE_REVIEW execute zero times.
Do not change tool-call default-allow behavior.
Do not change replay, audit or post-run evidence semantics.

acceptance: Ailuros exposes one narrow before_actor_substitution pre-action decision seam.
The API requires only role, opaque from/to identities, substitution reason, authority level and optional metadata.
A matching ALLOW policy authorizes the substitution.
No matching policy yields REQUIRE_REVIEW rather than implicit ALLOW.
WARN and SANITIZE cannot authorize actor substitution.
The resulting decision contains deterministic structured substitution evidence and input_hash.
GovernanceDecision, GovernanceDecisionType, Policy and DecisionResolver public semantics remain unchanged.
Existing governed tool behavior remains unchanged.
No fallback selection/execution, IAM, actor registry, model scoring or generic governance framework is introduced.
ruff, mypy, focused tests and full pytest pass.

must_check: The implementation provides a real pre-action actor-substitution decision API rather than only post-run detection.
ACTOR_SUBSTITUTION_REQUESTED evidence is persisted before the governance decision.
No matching substitution policy produces REQUIRE_REVIEW and allowed=false.
Explicit BLOCK produces BLOCK and allowed=false.
WARN and SANITIZE cannot fall through as authorization.
Existing GovernanceDecisionType, Policy schema and DecisionResolver global semantics are reused rather than redesigned.
Actor identities remain opaque runtime-supplied strings; Ailuros does not parse or score provider/model identity.
Ailuros does not select, start, retry or orchestrate the substitute actor.
Existing tool-call runtime enforcement tests still pass unchanged.
No forbidden files change and all validation commands pass.
reject_if: No-policy actor substitution defaults to ALLOW.
WARN or SANITIZE can cause a substitute actor to be considered authorized.
The implementation adds a new actor-specific decision enum or changes GovernanceDecisionType.
DecisionResolver's existing no-policy default is globally changed to make this feature work.
The Policy schema is expanded into an IAM/RBAC/ABAC or actor-permission system.
Provider/model names are parsed to infer authority, capability, trust or risk.
A model/provider trust score, ranking or fallback-selection mechanism is added.
Ailuros starts, retries, selects or otherwise orchestrates replacement actors.
Tool-specific event types are reused misleadingly for actor substitution.
The implementation generalizes into mutation/delegation/action governance without production evidence.
Validation fails or forbidden files change.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Pre-action authorization of runtime actor substitution using existing Ailuros policy and governance-decision primitives.
missing_targets: tests/test_actor_substitution_governance.py may be created by this pack
